title: Open-site cohomology comparisons and Zariski vanishing detection
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a finite commutative ring, and $T_\tau$ either its small etale or its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], using small representatives in a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A_T$ denote the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary unbounded derived category $D(T_\tau,A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^a$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be any set-indexed Zariski open cover of $T$.
For every open $U\subseteq T$, the functor $(V\to U)\mapsto(V\to T,V\to U)$ identifies $U_\tau$ with the localized site $T_\tau/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], including its topology. Under this identification there is a canonical ring isomorphism $A_U\cong A_T|_U$, the identity on constant sections, and restriction of module sheaves is the exact sectionwise functor $F|_U(V\to U)=F(V\to T)$. These identifications respect iterated open restriction. The family $(U_i\to T)$ is a cover on $T_\tau$, and for every object $V\to T$ its pullback $(V\times_T U_i\to V)$ is a cover on $V_\tau$ and on the corresponding localized site.
Writing $r_U$ for this exact restriction and $D(r_U)$ for its termwise derived functor [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], there are canonical isomorphisms
$$\chi^a_{U,K}:r_U\mathcal H^a(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^a(D(r_U)K)$$
for every $a\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in D(T_\tau,A)$. They are induced by the kernel, image and quotient comparisons, are natural for all derived morphisms, and agree with the composite comparisons for nested opens. For every module sheaf $F$ one has $F=0$ if and only if $r_{U_i}F=0$ for every $i$. Consequently, for every integer $a$,
$$\mathcal H^a(K)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathcal H^a(D(r_{U_i})K)=0\text{ for every }i.$$
These assertions include $T=\varnothing$ and the empty covering family; in that case every module sheaf is zero.

proof.text: Every inclusion of an open subscheme is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Since the images of the $U_i$ cover $T$, the family $(U_i\to T)$ is an etale covering by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and hence a pro-etale covering by [lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover]. The base-change covering axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] gives the covering $(V\times_T U_i\to V)$ for every object $V\to T$ of either site. Applying the same open-immersion and covering assertions with base $V$ shows it also covers on $V_\tau$. In the slice over $V$ its underlying family is this same covering, so it covers there by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. This argument applies to arbitrary set-indexed covers, without assuming quasi-compactness of $T$.

source.place: Tag 098B, lemma-etale-proetale; sites.tex Definition 00VH, definition-site, covering base-change axiom

proof.text: For an open $U\subseteq T$, its inclusion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] to obtain precisely the stated functor $U_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq T_{\mathrm{et}}/U$, including its covering families. In the pro-etale case apply [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], which explicitly includes open subschemes, gives the same functor, and identifies the covering families. Work first on the common bounded-object categories, then transport to the chosen small representatives; these are the same sites up to the equivalences specified in the statement. For nested opens $W\subseteq U\subseteq T$ both composites send $V\to W$ to its composite $V\to T$ with its factorization through $U$. Relocalization in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] therefore gives the specified coherent identifications of sites.

source.place: Section 00XZ, section-localize; Lemma 03EH, lemma-relocalize; pro-etale specialization as in proetale.tex Definition 098K, definition-big-small-proetale

proof.text: Let $P$ be the constant presheaf of rings with value $A$. Its restriction to the slice is again the constant presheaf with value $A$. By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and the ring-valued comparison [lem-pur-ring-presheaf-sheafification-localization], $(P|_U)^\#\xrightarrow{\sim}(P^\#)|_U$ is the required $A_U\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T|_U$. The unit equation in that comparison says explicitly that the image of each constant section $a\in A$ is unchanged. For nested opens, the direct map and the composite of the two restricted maps agree after precomposition with the constant-presheaf unit. The uniqueness in the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] makes the two sheaf maps equal. Thus the coefficient comparison is canonical and respects iterated restriction in both topologies.

source.place: Tag 00XR, lemma-when-shriek, applied to localization Section 00XZ; sheafification universal property Tag 00WH, proposition-sheafification-adjoint

proof.text: On the localized ringed site, [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] gives $r_UF(V\to U)=F(V\to T)$ and gives the same formula for morphisms and the scalar action. The coefficient identification of Step 3 makes this an $A_U$-module sheaf on $U_\tau$. The exactness assertion of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], applied to the sheaf of rings $A_T$ and the object $U$, proves exactness of this module restriction. The categories are abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; the small representatives and common coefficient universe assumed in the item meet its size condition. Relocalization gives $(F|_U)|_W=F|_W$ sectionwise, and Step 3 shows their scalar identifications agree as well.

source.place: Tag 04IX, definition-localize-ringed-site (4); restriction exactness for the localization morphism; sites.tex Lemma 03EH, lemma-relocalize

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to the exact functor $r_U$. For every cochain complex $C$ its canonical natural comparison, inverted, gives $r_UH^a(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^a(r_UC)$, induced by kernels, images and quotients. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], termwise $r_U$ induces $D(r_U)$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. The localization description in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] lets the preceding comparison descend: it is natural for each chain map; for a quasi-isomorphism its naturality square has invertible vertical arrows, so the square for its inverse also commutes. Morphisms of the localization are generated by these maps and their composites, and naturality is preserved by composition. This proves naturality for every derived morphism and gives the asserted $\chi^a_{U,K}$, independent of the chosen complex representative. No resolution or boundedness assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, all complexes compute the derived functor; homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor

proof.text: For $W\subseteq U\subseteq T$, compare the direct $\chi^a_W$ with $\chi^a_{W,D(r_U)(-)}\circ r_{W/U}(\chi^a_U)$, under the restriction identifications of Steps 2--4. On a complex both maps are induced by the same inclusion of cycles into the restricted degree-$a$ term and the same quotient by the restricted boundaries. Uniqueness of the induced kernel and quotient maps forces equality. The comparison lemma [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] specifies exactly these kernel/image-induced maps. Hence equality holds on all complex representatives and therefore on the derived category as in Step 5. This verifies the stated iterated cohomology comparison, rather than choosing unrelated isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, canonical kernel and cokernel maps; sites.tex Lemma 03EH, lemma-relocalize

proof.text: Suppose $r_{U_i}F=0$ for every $i$. For each object $V\to T$, Step 1 supplies the covering $(V\times_T U_i\to V)$. Its section modules are $F(V\times_T U_i)=(r_{U_i}F)(V\times_T U_i\to U_i)=0$ by the restriction formula [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The underlying abelian sheaf of a module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] satisfies the equalizer sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; in particular $F(V)\to\prod_i F(V\times_T U_i)$ is injective. The product is the zero module, so $F(V)=0$. This holds for every $V$, hence $F$ is the zero module sheaf. Conversely the sectionwise restriction of the zero sheaf has zero section modules, so is zero. This proves both directions for either site without any stalk or point hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 00VM and 00VR, definition-sheaf-sets and definition-sheaf, equalizer sheaf axiom

proof.text: For fixed $a$ apply Step 7 to the module sheaf $F=\mathcal H^a(K)$. The isomorphisms of Step 5 identify the vanishing of $r_{U_i}F$ with that of $\mathcal H^a(D(r_{U_i})K)$, giving exactly the asserted equivalence. Finally if $T=\varnothing$, every scheme admitting a morphism to $T$ is empty. On either site the empty family covers each such object: joint surjectivity is vacuous in the etale definition [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and the pro-etale assertion follows from Step 1 with this empty etale family. The equalizer sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] says $F(V)$ is the equalizer of two maps between empty products, hence the zero module. Thus every module sheaf is zero, also for the empty covering family. If $T$ is nonempty the empty family is not a Zariski cover, so no assertion for that family is needed.
